citations.narrative:
On 26 April 2026, a Harris' antelope squirrel was found to sustain a non-life threatening bleeding injury to the right foot
from the metal exercise wheel in their enclosure. The animal received veterinary treatment and the exercise wheel was
replaced with a safer designed plastic structure. Housing animals in facilities not appropriate for the species may result in
injuries. The indoor housing facilities shall be structurally sound and constructed of materials appropriate for the animals
to protect them from injury. Corrected prior to inspection.
Correct from this date forward of 11 September 2026.

On 02 July 2026, an adult cedar waxwing was found deceased and trapped between the interior shade screen and metal
fencing of an outdoor enclosure. The facility had notified the inspector of the event and removed the shade screen from
the enclosure housing additional birds. The bird's necropsy report listed trauma as the first possible diagnosis. Not
providing housing for birds that protects them from injury can result in circumstances leading to death. Housing facilities
for birds must be designed, constructed and maintained in good repair so that they protect the birds from injury. Corrected
prior to inspection.
Correct from this date forward of 11 September 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
